title: K80 iOS 26 native QTB, SMMU bank and peer stream integration candidate
changes: Rebased the v61 native reserveActual bank allocator onto the later native QTB power/resume source. It keeps the controller-claim and live register census checks; it only reserves the software bank ledger and does not program bank or stream registers.

Reapplied the peer-aware activation change to both GPU SMMU endpoints. The second activation validates the first endpoint's exact prepared/active transition while re-reading the complete stream table.

The QTB source retains its actual child/provider/resource lookup, TBU power and normal resume path, and guarded native cold-MMIO backend. Its independent cold-controller hardware grant remains external and mandatory.

compile.warning_set: same HoujiFullHostNativeMemory.h narrowing warnings as QTB power/resume base

qualification_limits: This is an offline, unselected link. It was not packaged, booted or accessed on the device.

The external acquireActualStream authority still must serialize the full effective match set and prove real GPU/GMU producer quiescence or fault control. Peer-state validation and the QTB fence ACK are not that lease.
The actual GPU startup-owner factory is still not connected to the direct-ring platform call path, and independent SMMU mapping/page-table ownership remains required.
No stream or context-bank register write, DMA, SMMU translation, GMU firmware/HFI, GPU execution, fence or Metal rendering is established.
next_action: Bind a real K80 GPU and GMU producer gate across the full effective stream match set; establish independent mapping ownership; connect the real startup owner to direct-ring before preparing a hardware trial.
